findings.title: Imported embed content is stored and rendered as raw HTML without sanitization
findings.body: TopicEmbed.import creates posts with skip_validations and cook_method Post.cook_methods[:raw_html], so Post#cook returns the imported feed/readability HTML unchanged. The embed view renders post.cooked with raw. Untrusted RSS/Atom or scraped content can therefore contain script tags, event handlers, or javascript: URLs, leading to stored XSS in Discourse and embedding pages.

findings.title: Import footer interpolates the embed URL into HTML without escaping
findings.body: TopicEmbed.import appends an imported-from footer containing #{url} to the content before saving it as raw HTML. The only validation is that the URL starts with http(s)://, so quotes, angle brackets, or script-bearing URL components can inject markup into the post.

findings.title: request.referer is embedded in inline JavaScript without escaping
findings.body: The embed layout outputs request.referer directly inside a script string for parent.postMessage. A Referer header containing a single quote or other script-breaking characters can inject JavaScript into the Discourse embed page. The value should be JSON/JS-escaped or replaced with a validated origin.

findings.title: Invalid ERB end tag will break template compilation
findings.body: The first conditional in best.html.erb is closed with <%- end if %>, which compiles to invalid Ruby syntax. Rendering this template will raise a syntax error. It should be closed with a normal ERB end tag.

findings.title: Unknown embed URLs trigger background retrieval without validating the URL host
findings.body: EmbedController#best only validates the Referer host, then enqueues :retrieve_topic for any embed_url parameter. The embed_url host is only checked later inside TopicRetriever. This allows a client that can present an acceptable Referer to enqueue many jobs for arbitrary URLs, causing Sidekiq load and unwanted fetch attempts. Validate and/or throttle embed_url before enqueuing.

findings.title: Feed item content is assumed present
findings.body: poll_feed calls i.content.scrub for every feed item. Many feeds provide only description/summary or may have nil content, in which case SimpleRSS returns nil and the job raises NoMethodError, aborting the entire poll. It should fall back safely to other item fields.

findings.title: Feed fetch has no timeout or error handling
findings.body: SimpleRSS.parse open(SiteSetting.feed_polling_url) uses open-uri without timeouts, redirect controls, or rescue for network and parse errors. A slow, unreachable, or malformed feed can hang or crash the scheduled job.

findings.title: Redis throttle uses non-atomic SETNX + EXPIRE
findings.body: retrieved_recently? calls $redis.setnx and then $redis.expire. If the process crashes between those calls, or expire fails, the key remains without a TTL and that embed URL can be throttled forever. Use an atomic SET with NX and EX, or another safe Redis pattern.

findings.title: Missing embed URLs trigger a full synchronous feed poll
findings.body: perform_retrieve executes Jobs::PollFeed.new.execute({}) inline whenever a single unknown embed URL is requested and feed polling is enabled. Each distinct unknown URL can force a complete fetch and import of the configured feed, which is expensive and can be abused. The feed poll should be debounced or enqueued asynchronously.

findings.title: content_sha1 is updated even if the revision fails
findings.body: In the update branch, TopicEmbed.import calls PostRevisor#revise! and then unconditionally updates the embed content_sha1. If the revision/save fails or returns false, the stored SHA will no longer match the post body and future legitimate content changes may be skipped.

findings.title: Post creation success is checked with present? instead of persisted?
findings.body: After PostCreator#create, TopicEmbed.import checks if post.present?. PostCreator can return an unsaved Post object with errors after a rollback, so this condition can be true for a non-persisted post. The subsequent TopicEmbed.create! can then fail on nil topic_id/post_id or create inconsistent data. Check post.persisted? and errors before creating the embed.

findings.title: TopicEmbed records are not cleaned up when topic or post are deleted
findings.body: TopicEmbed belongs_to :topic and :post but has no dependent destroy or cleanup callback. If a topic or post is destroyed, stale topic_embed rows remain. topic_id_for_embed can then return a deleted topic id, and update code may later call methods on a nil post.

findings.title: PostCreator jobs are enqueued inside the outer Topic.transaction
findings.body: TopicEmbed.import wraps PostCreator#create in a Topic.transaction. PostCreator enqueues background jobs after its own Post.transaction block, but that block is nested inside the outer transaction, so jobs may be queued before the topic/embed data is committed. Workers can race and fail to see the new records.

findings.title: Remote import fetch has no timeout or failure handling
findings.body: TopicEmbed.import_remote calls open(url).read without timeouts or error handling. A slow or failing remote host can hang the retrieve-topic worker. This fetch should use explicit timeouts and rescue network errors.

findings.title: postMessage origin check uses substring matching
findings.body: The resize listener accepts messages if discourseUrl.indexOf(e.origin) === -1 is false. This substring test can match origins that are prefixes or otherwise embedded in the discourseUrl string. Use an exact origin comparison after normalizing scheme/host/port.

findings.title: Default-port handling is scheme-independent
findings.body: absolutize_urls omits the port whenever it is 80 or 443, regardless of URI scheme. For http://host:443/ or https://host:80/, it will generate URLs without the required port. Compare the port against the default port for the URI scheme instead.

findings.title: Template assumes post.user is present
findings.body: The embed/best view calls post.user.small_avatar_url and post.user.username without nil checks. Posts can have missing or deleted users, which will cause a NoMethodError when rendering the embedded topic.

findings.title: create_table with force: true can drop an existing table
findings.body: Changing this migration to create_table :top_topics, force: true means the migration will drop the top_topics table if it already exists. If this migration is rerun or run against a database where the table was created previously, data can be lost. Use a new migration or conditional DDL instead.
